sectionProgressions.description: Four-bar classical nylon descending progression with suspended upper chord melody
Rich circle-of-fifths voice leading with half-diminished ii chord leading to major dominant V7
Expands into fuller fingerpicked textures supporting Sting's contemplative vocal

harmonicFunction: F#m (i) - Somber minor tonic established with low 2nd-fret bass note
E6 (VII6) - First stepwise bass drop (F# → E) providing smooth classical continuity
D6 (VI6) - Second stepwise bass drop (E → D) maintaining harmonic descent
C#7 (V7) - Classical major dominant containing the E# leading tone pulling decisively back into F#m
G#m7b5 (iiø7) - Half-diminished chord providing sophisticated jazz/classical transition to V7

techniques.name: Classical Nylon-String PIMA Arpeggiation
techniques.description: Using classical thumb-index-middle-ring (PIMA) fingerpicking to cleanly articulate bass notes on the beat while weaving intricate arpeggio patterns on strings 2, 3, and 4

notes: Bass notes: F# (2nd fret low E), E (open low E), D (5th fret A string), C# (4th fret A string)
Inner voices: Ringing dyads on strings 4, 3, and 2
Delicate finger pressure to prevent fret buzz on nylon or acoustic strings
sequence: Pluck the low F# bass note with the thumb (P)
Follow with index (I) on string 4, middle (M) on string 3, and ring (A) on string 2
Shift bass notes smoothly on beats 1 and 3 without interrupting upper voice sustain
Nail the stretch on the G#m7b5 chord shape
tips: Play near the soundhole (tasto) for a round, warm classical tone
Keep your right-hand thumb positioned forward of your fingers to prevent collisions
Dominic Miller composed this on a nylon-string classical guitar—nylon string tension makes the wide stretches easier

sections.name: Main Classical Arpeggio

notes: Let the bass notes ring as pedal tones

notes: Fret G#m7b5 with index on 4th fret low E and ring on 4th fret D
Smooth resolution to the C#7 shape

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Bass Descent
steps: Learn the four fundamental chord shapes: F#m, E, D, and C#7
Practice the descending bassline on the lower strings (F# → E → D → C#)
Play simple thumb-and-finger strums at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: PIMA Fingerpicking Pattern
steps: Internalize the exact thumb-index-middle-ring fingerpicking cycle
Coordinate the shifting bass notes with continuous upper-string arpeggios
Smoothly execute the transition into the G#m7b5 chord

advanced.title: Concert Fluency & Tone Nuance
steps: Play the entire 4-minute composition with fluid classical touch and zero buzzing
Control dynamic swell between quiet verses and expressive chorus peaks
Perform cleanly on nylon strings without relying on heavy compression

commonMistakes: Rushing the tempo (keep it strictly at 84 BPM)
Collapsing your right-hand wrist causing the fingernails to click against strings
Muting the high notes during the wide fret stretch on the G#m7b5 chord
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Right-hand PIMA arpeggio drill on open strings
5 minutes: First 4-bar progression shifting with metronome at 70 BPM
5 minutes: G#m7b5 turnaround stretch isolated practice
5 minutes: Complete playthrough with attention to tone warmth
focusAreas: Clean string separation without fret buzz
metronomeWork: Practice at 65 BPM with steady 8th-note clicks to build finger coordination
Advance to 84 BPM ensuring bass notes land precisely on beats 1 and 3
